H&P – Detailed

Consult Summary:
53-year-old man with 1-week history of painless swelling and warmth over the left elbow; clinical impression is olecranon bursitis. NSAID therapy started and blood tests arranged; safety-netting given.

History:
• Presenting complaint – Soft, fluctuant swelling noted over left elbow 1 week ago while showering.  
• Course – Size and warmth persist; no significant pain; full range of motion; no prior episodes.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors – None identified; no trauma or repetitive strain; desk-based job.  
• Associated symptoms – Mild local warmth, mild peri-bursal tenderness; no systemic symptoms, no skin rash elsewhere, no fever, no significant redness, no limitation of movement.  
• Review of systems – Denies eczema; otherwise well.  

Past Medical History:
• Osteoarthritis – GP-diagnosed several years ago; joints occasionally painful; no current complications noted.  

Medications:
• None on a regular basis.  
Allergies:
• Peanuts – allergic.  
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Occupation – Desk-based work.  
• Exercise – Runs 2–3 times/week; generally active and fit.  
• No smoking, alcohol, or substance history documented.

Family History:
• No known family history of rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, or other rheumatological disease.

Physical Examination:
(Virtual video assessment)  
• General – Well-appearing, comfortable.  
• Left elbow – Visible swelling over olecranon; mildly warm to touch; skin over tip appears dry; non-tender at olecranon tip, mild tenderness adjacent to swelling; full active range of motion; no marked erythema.  
• No other joint abnormalities visualised.  
• Vitals – Not provided.

Investigations:
• Planned: Blood tests for inflammatory markers (ESR/CRP), infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, uric acid (gout screen). Forms to be mailed to patient.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected olecranon bursitis (non-septic)  
• Start ibuprofen 400 mg orally twice daily after food (OTC).  
• Advise to stop if gastrointestinal side-effects occur.  
• Arrange blood tests as above to evaluate for underlying inflammatory or infectious etiology.  
• Follow-up (video or face-to-face) after results (~6 days); clinician to review swelling and labs.  
• Safety-net: Seek urgent care if elbow becomes very red, increasingly painful, swelling spreads, or systemic symptoms develop (rule-out septic arthritis).

General Plan items:  
• Provide patient information on olecranon bursitis and NSAID use.  
• Encourage continued gentle activity; avoid direct pressure on elbow.  
• Document allergy and medication status at next visit.

Quality checks:

• Missing expected elements – No vitals, no comprehensive medication reconciliation beyond patient statement.  
• Internal conflicts – None noted.  
• Transcript quality – Clear; minor conversational noise but clinically adequate.
